sentence_stem: The results of the test will be announced
correct_completion: next Friday, once all the papers have been checked.
full_sentence: The results of the test will be announced next Friday, once all the papers have been checked.
acceptable_variants: next Friday, after all the papers have been marked.
next Friday, when the marking has been finished.

options.text: next Friday, once all the papers have check.
options.why_wrong: 'Have check' is missing the past participle; the passive needs 'have been checked'.

options.text: next Friday, once all the papers have been checked.
next Friday, once all the papers was checked.
options.why_wrong: 'Was' does not agree with the plural subject 'papers', and the present perfect passive needs 'have been'.

options.text: next Friday, once all the papers be checked.
options.why_wrong: The auxiliary 'be' needs 'have' before it, so the correct form is 'have been checked'.

grammar_focus: Present perfect passive: have been + past participle
explanation: The passive with 'have been' + past participle describes an action completed before the announcement. Portuguese speakers may use an active verb or a simple past here, because the English passive with 'have been' is not structured the same way in their language.
translation: Os resultados do teste serão anunciados na próxima sexta-feira, assim que todas as provas tiverem sido corrigidas.
